en.title: Nautus Swims into View: A Steamworld Dig Meets Subnautica Survival Adventure
en.summary: Get ready for a delightfully weird aquatic adventure! Nautus, from the makers of Have a Nice Death, is blending cozy island life with deep-sea Metroidvania survival.
en.body:
Prepare to dive into a world where the sun-drenched surface hides the secrets of a mysterious ocean floor. **Nautus**, the latest creation from **Magic Design Studios**, the minds behind the charmingly gothic **Have a Nice Death**, is gearing up to offer players a truly unique blend of cozy island living and Metroidvania-inspired underwater exploration.

Imagine a tranquil tropical getaway, reminiscent of classic Cartoon Network animation, where your primary goal is to reconnect with your community and uncover the enigma of a lost uncle. This is the surface-level charm of **Nautus**. Players will find themselves on a faraway island, engaging with quirky, chill locals who are working to rebuild their lives. The initial gameplay loop is designed to be atmospheric and comforting, inviting players to settle in and embrace the routine of island life. However, the true adventure beckons beneath the waves. Once you gain access to your submersible, the game shifts gears dramatically, transforming into a survival-action experience where danger and discovery await in the deep.

This duality is precisely what makes **Nautus** so intriguing. The developers themselves have described it as feeling like a mash-up between the methodical digging and upgrading of **Steamworld Dig** and the vast, often perilous exploration of **Subnautica**. While the surface offers a cozy, community-focused experience, the underwater realms demand careful resource management, strategic navigation, and a keen eye for potential threats. It’s a bold move to combine such disparate gameplay styles, but if **Magic Design Studios** can pull it off, **Nautus** could offer a gaming experience unlike any other.

## Beneath the Waves: A Metroidvania Mystery

The underwater exploration in **Nautus** is where the game truly flexes its muscles. As players venture deeper, they’ll need to upgrade their mini-submarine to withstand the increasing pressures and uncover the island's long-held secrets. This section of the game is heavily influenced by Metroidvania design principles, suggesting a world that opens up as you acquire new abilities and gear. The blend of survival mechanics with the non-linear exploration typical of the genre promises a compelling loop of challenge and reward. It’s this underwater mystery, coupled with the charming world-building, that will likely hook players looking for something beyond typical cozy fare.

> "It's essentially Jacques Cousteau by way of The Adventures of Flapjack. Nautus feels, in many ways, like a careful mash-up between Steamworld Dig and Subnautica."

This description from the preview perfectly encapsulates the ambitious scope of **Nautus**. It promises a world that is both familiar and alien, comforting and challenging, all wrapped in a distinctive visual style.

## What This Means for Fans

For fans of **Magic Design Studios**, this is a fascinating evolution. Moving from the cutesy-gothic setting of **Have a Nice Death** to a more folksy, tropical environment with deep-sea secrets shows a willingness to experiment and push creative boundaries. Players who enjoyed the studio's previous work will likely be drawn to the unique art style and character design, while the shift to a survival-action core will appeal to a broader audience. The promise of a cozy game that also delivers thrilling underwater exploration taps into the growing market for games that offer both relaxation and excitement, proving that chill vibes don't have to mean a lack of challenge.

## What's Next

**Nautus** is slated for a closed beta launch soon, with the full game expected to release following its appearance at Gamescom 2026. Keep an eye out for more details on when you can get your hands on this intriguing aquatic adventure.

Gameplay above the surface is cozy, but when you take your submersible under the sea, it becomes a Metroidvania-inspired survival-action game. To be a cozy game is to embrace all things chill and atmospheric, finding comfort in routine and bonding with a growing community of characters, taking it one day at a time. With the upcoming Nautus from developer Magic Design Studios, it's bringing those chill vibes to a tropical island setting where the waters below hide long-held secrets, and some quirky friends will help you uncover them. It's a delightfully weird concept with some interesting ideas, all channeled in the style of a classic Cartoon Network animated show that brings the world to life. Just ahead of Gamescom 2026 and the upcoming closed-beta launch, we got some hands-on time with Nautus and its offbeat aquatic world filled with deep-sea wonders. Along with some solid playtime, we also got to speak with game designer Damian Carmona about the making of Nautus, and how they're following up on Have a Nice Death's cutesy-gothic setting of the afterlife with a new world that's a bit more folksy and tropical and has many underwater secrets to uncover. Nautus and its re brought to the seemingly tranquil faraway island in search of your lost uncle. After meeting the strange-but-totally-chill locals who are trying to get their community back on its feet, you're soon given access to an underwater submersible that can steadily explore the waters below. But to reach the lowest depths to uncover the mystery of the island and the underwater world, you'll need to power up your mini-submarine and empower the community on the surface to make it happen. "We're very proud of Have a Nice Death, but we wanted to change it a little bit from the gothic style and the black and white visuals to go for something a bit more The developer's previous work on the cult-hit 2D action-roguelike Have a Nice Death – another game with a charming, cartoon-inspired visual style – was something of a stepping stone for their turn to Nautus, but mostly for the new opportunity to go for something more We're going on very different adventures with Nautus, when it comes to tone and all that. We're very proud of Have a Nice Death, but we wanted to change it a little bit from the gothic style and the black and white visuals to go for something a bit more said the game director. "We said, 'Hey, let's make a game in this ocean setting.' It just came to life with a lot of interactions with the world, and of course for the survival, crafting, and exploration gameplay as well."
